claims.statement: A Zoom Server-to-Server OAuth app has a client secret, displayed with the account ID and client ID in the app credentials section of the app, which the developer uses to authenticate with Zoom.

sources.supports: App credentials - View your account ID, client ID and client secret. You'll use these credentials to authenticate with Zoom.
sources.locator: Steps to create a Server-to-Server OAuth app, app credentials item

sources.supports: App credentials are the client credentials, including the account ID, client ID, and client secret, which Zoom provides to app developers to access the Zoom platform.

claims.statement: Zoom's Server-to-Server OAuth page says to Base64 encode the client ID and client secret with a colon between them and send them using the Basic HTTP Authentication Scheme in the Authorization header of a POST to https://zoom.us/oauth/token with grant_type account_credentials and the account_id in the body; the OAuth reference repeats it for the Server to Server app type.

sources.supports: Encode the client ID and client secret in base64 format (with a colon between them, e.g. client_id:client_secret). Set up your API request header and include your encoded client ID and client secret using the 'Basic' HTTP Authentication Scheme
sources.locator: Generate access token, To generate an access token, steps 1 and 2

sources.supports: Send the header and body as a POST request to the token API at https://zoom.us/oauth/token to get an access token.
sources.locator: Generate access token, To generate an access token, step 4

sources.supports: To request an access token, send a POST request to https://zoom.us/oauth/token. Include a basic authorization header ... The basic authorization header is your Client ID and Client Secret with a colon : in between, Base64 Encoded.
sources.locator: Request an access token, App Type: Server to Server

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Not researched beyond existence: prefix, alphabet, length and any checksum are not stated on the pages read, and no value shape may be inferred from the examples (docs examples are placeholders or illustrative).

The account ID and client ID sit beside the secret in the same credentials section; the pages read do not say whether they are treated as secret. They are not recorded as secrets and need a sibling-level reading in research-family.

The pages read describe a general client secret (app-credentials page) and the Server-to-Server one in the same terms; whether they are one credential family or two is not settled here (see zoom:oauth-app-client-secret).
The Basic envelope encodes the secret together with the public client ID; no prefix, alphabet or width of the secret is stated and the example Basic values are placeholders, not a format.
